name: Set 3: Bushveld & Backroads
description: Super Rugby, Rock Anthems, Big Five Wildlife & Safari Roads

questions.q: Which fruit is traditionally used to garnish a classic Gin & Tonic cocktail?
questions.fact: Crisp lime wedge or slice of lemon is the standard garnish.

questions.q: How many millimeters are there in a standard metric meter?
questions.fact: 1,000 millimeters per meter.

questions.q: Which animal is featured on the famous label of Castle Milk Stout?
questions.fact: The iconic black bull with horns symbolizing rich malt strength.

questions.q: What board game involves buying streets like Mayfair, building green houses, and collecting 200 for passing GO?
questions.fact: Monopoly, originally published in its modern form by Parker Brothers in 1935.

questions.q: How many days are there in a leap year?
questions.fact: February 29 gives a leap year 366 days.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.fact: Canberra was selected in 1908 as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.q: In South African slang, if someone says 'nou-nou', roughly when do they mean?
answers: Sometime in the near or distant future
questions.fact: Nou-nou is generally later than 'nou' (now), but sooner than 'later'!

questions.q: How many strings does a standard acoustic or electric guitar typically have?
questions.fact: Tuned E-A-D-G-B-E.

questions.q: Which planet in our solar system is nicknamed 'The Red Planet'?
questions.fact: Iron oxide (rust) on Mars's surface gives it a reddish hue.

questions.q: What is the main spirit used to make a classic Margarita cocktail?
questions.fact: Tequila, triple sec, and fresh lime juice, traditionally served with a salted rim.

questions.q: Which South African golfer is nicknamed 'The Big Easy' for his smooth, effortless swing?
questions.round: Round 2 · World Cups, Derbies & Golf Legends
questions.fact: Ernie Els won four Major championships: two US Opens and two Open Championships.

questions.q: Which legendary South African golfer won nine Major championships and is one of only five players to win the career Grand Slam?
questions.round: Round 2 · World Cups, Derbies & Golf Legends
questions.fact: Gary Player: 'The Black Knight', with 9 Major victories.

questions.q: In Super Rugby history, which South African franchise won the championship three times (2007, 2009, 2010)?
questions.round: Round 2 · World Cups, Derbies & Golf Legends
questions.fact: The Bulls won thrilling finals under coach Frans Ludeke and captain Victor Matfield.

questions.q: In football (soccer), which two Soweto giants contest the famous 'Soweto Derby'?
questions.round: Round 2 · World Cups, Derbies & Golf Legends
questions.fact: One of the most fiercely contested derby matches in world soccer, packing FNB Stadium.

questions.q: Which Springbok flyhalf kicked 100% of his goal kicks across the 2023 Rugby World Cup knockout stage?
questions.round: Round 2 · World Cups, Derbies & Golf Legends
questions.fact: Pollard had ice in his veins, slotting winning penalties against France, England, and New Zealand.

questions.q: In cricket, how many runs are awarded when a batsman hits the ball over the boundary rope on the full without bouncing?
questions.round: Round 2 · World Cups, Derbies & Golf Legends
questions.fact: A maximum: 6 runs on the full.

questions.q: Which famous stadium in Durban was renowned for rugby fans braaiing on 'The Shark Tank' outer fields?
questions.round: Round 2 · World Cups, Derbies & Golf Legends
questions.fact: Home of the Sharks rugby team.

questions.q: Which South African swimmer won the Olympic Gold medal in the 100m breaststroke at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics?
questions.round: Round 2 · World Cups, Derbies & Golf Legends
questions.fact: Penny Heyns made history by winning both the 100m and 200m breaststroke golds in Atlanta.

questions.q: What is the regulation number of holes played in a full round of golf?
questions.round: Round 2 · World Cups, Derbies & Golf Legends
questions.fact: St Andrews in Scotland standardized the 18-hole golf course in 1764.

questions.q: Which country won the inaugural Rugby World Cup in 1987?
questions.round: Round 2 · World Cups, Derbies & Golf Legends
questions.fact: The All Blacks defeated France 29-9 at Eden Park, Auckland.

questions.q: Which legendary British rock band recorded the operatic masterpiece 'Bohemian Rhapsody' in 1975?
questions.fact: Fronted by Freddie Mercury, on their album A Night at the Opera.

questions.q: In the 1984 sci-fi action film The Terminator, what is Arnold Schwarzenegger's immortal five-word catchphrase?
questions.fact: 'I'll be back' was spoken at the police precinct desk before he drives a car through the front doors.

questions.q: Which South African rock band had huge hits in the late 90s and 2000s with songs like 'Bubblegum On My Sole' and 'Genie'?
questions.fact: Fronted by Arno Carstens, formed in Stellenbosch in 1994.

questions.q: In the 1994 Disney animated film The Lion King, what Swahili phrase translates literally to 'No worries'?
questions.fact: Sung by Timon and Pumbaa.

questions.q: Which Australian hard rock band released the timeless 1980 rock anthem 'Back in Black'?
questions.fact: Their first album featuring new singer Brian Johnson following Bon Scott's death.

questions.q: In the Lord of the Rings trilogy, what creature continuously refers to the One Ring as 'My Precious'?
questions.fact: Portrayed by Andy Serkis via groundbreaking motion capture.

questions.q: What British spy's signature cocktail order is a vodka martini, 'shaken, not stirred'?
questions.fact: Agent 007 created by author Ian Fleming.

questions.q: Which American singer-songwriter released the record-breaking 1982 album Thriller, featuring 'Beat It' and 'Billie Jean'?
questions.fact: Thriller remains the best-selling studio album of all time.

questions.q: In the 1994 hit movie Forrest Gump, what did Forrest's mama always say life was like?
questions.fact: 'You never know what you're gonna get.'

questions.q: Which South African alt-rock band fronted by Francois van Coke created shockwaves in 2003 with their raw Afrikaans punk?
questions.fact: Formed in Bellville, Western Cape in 2003.

questions.q: What uniquely South African steakhouse condiment, made with chutney, tomato sauce, and Worcestershire sauce, was invented by Johannesburg chefs in the 1960s?
questions.fact: Created by overseas hotel chefs at the Carlton Hotel in Johannesburg; contains zero actual monkeys!

questions.q: Which famous wine-producing town in the Western Cape is renowned for its Cape Dutch architecture and prestigious university?
questions.fact: Founded in 1679 by Simon van der Stel; South Africa's premier wine center.

questions.q: What is the key difference between biltong and American beef jerky?
answers: Biltong is cured in vinegar and air-dried; jerky is typically heat-smoked and dried
Biltong is only made from pork
questions.fact: Biltong uses vinegar, salt, and spices, air-drying gently without smoke or artificial cooking.

questions.q: What French term is used for sparkling wines produced in South Africa using the traditional Champagne method?
questions.fact: MCC refers to bottle-fermented sparkling wine made in South Africa.

questions.q: Which cut of steak is famous for featuring a T-shaped bone separating a strip loin from a smaller tenderloin fillet?
questions.fact: A T-bone contains both sirloin and tenderloin fillet on either side of the bone.

questions.q: What sweet dessert, made of a rich spongy cake covered in warm butter-caramel sauce, is a Sunday braai staple in South Africa?
questions.fact: Contains apricot jam in the batter, soaked in warm sweet cream sauce.

questions.q: In a bar, what spirit forms the alcoholic foundation of an Irish Coffee?
questions.fact: Hot black coffee, Irish whiskey, sugar, and float of fresh cream.

questions.q: What popular spicy South African vegetable relish consists of grated carrots, peppers, beans, and curry spices?
questions.fact: Originated in the townships of Johannesburg to accompany pap and braaivleis.

questions.q: Which popular style of beer is characterized by the acronym 'IPA'?
questions.fact: Heavily hopped beer brewed originally in Britain for export to colonial troops in India.

questions.q: What twisted, plaited South African pastry is deep-fried, dipped straight into ice-cold sugar syrup, and eaten cold?
questions.fact: Sticky, crunchy, sweet heaven! (The Cape Malay version is a spiced doughnut rolled in coconut).

questions.q: Which five animals traditionally make up Africa's famous 'Big Five'?
answers: Leopard, Cheetah, Wild Dog, Elephant, Hippo
questions.fact: Originally coined by big-game hunters as the five most dangerous animals to hunt on foot.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Canada?
questions.fact: Ottawa was chosen by Queen Victoria in 1857 as Canada's capital.

questions.q: In which province is the world-renowned Kruger National Park primarily located?
questions.fact: Stretches across both Limpopo and Mpumalanga along the Mozambique border.

questions.q: What spectacular waterfall on the Zambezi River between Zambia and Zimbabwe is known locally as 'Mosi-oa-Tunya' (The Smoke That Thunders)?
questions.fact: One of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World.

questions.q: What is the highest mountain peak in Africa, located in northeastern Tanzania?
questions.fact: Stands 5,895 meters above sea level.

questions.q: What is the capital city of France?
questions.fact: The City of Light, home to the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre.

questions.q: Which mammal is known as the fastest land animal in the world, capable of sprinting over 100 km/h?
questions.fact: Cheetahs can accelerate from 0 to 95 km/h in under 3 seconds.

questions.q: Which South African bay along the Garden Route is renowned globally as one of the best land-based whale-watching spots?
questions.fact: Southern Right Whales visit Walker Bay in Hermanus from June to November.

questions.q: What is the largest hot desert in the world, stretching across northern Africa?
questions.fact: Spanning over 9 million square kilometers.

questions.q: What famous road along the Atlantic seaboard of Cape Town is carved into the cliffs between Hout Bay and Noordhoek?
questions.fact: Affectionately called 'Chappies', featuring 114 curves over 9 kilometers.

questions.q: How many total kilometers of fence surround the perimeter of the Kruger National Park?
questions.fact: Approximately 1,000 km of boundary fencing.

questions.q: In what calendar year did South Africa win its second Rugby World Cup in Paris under captain John Smit?
questions.fact: 20 October 2007: Springboks 15 - England 6.

questions.q: How many total test runs did Jacques Kallis score in his international Test cricket career?
questions.fact: Jacques Kallis scored 13,289 runs in 166 Test matches.
